Welfare walks peak rules
Everyone on the desk should know one way of working
Companion Animal Travel Desk - customer care and safe handling
This section guides how we keep animal travel calm, clear, and kind for every passenger and pet. We give simple advice before departure, check carrier needs early, and make sure the ground team moves each animal with steady care. If a traveler arrives worried, we slow down, listen, and explain the next step in plain language.

We treat every booking as a welfare matter first. That means we confirm documents, carrier fit, and feeding notes without rushing, and we pass any concern to the senior coordinator as soon as it appears. When a pet lounge matter comes up, <<FACT F019>> we keep the conversation focused on comfort, handover, and the passenger's confidence. Staff should also share updates with the ramp team in a calm tone so the animal is not startled by noise or sudden movement.

When demand rises, we still protect patience and space for each animal. <<FACT F008>> If a kennel looks cramped, a pet seems distressed, or a carrier is damaged, we pause the move and review the case step by step. We do not promise a fix before checking what the animal needs, and we never let speed override welfare. Escalations should follow the calm chain of review, with the desk logging facts clearly and keeping the passenger informed.

If anything feels uncertain, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor right away.
